messages.author: 855a0980fb1d11d7
messages.subject: Confidence intervals
parts:
Dear Authors

Is there any way to calculate a confidence interval on either the estimated methylation difference and/or on the average methylation in each group as calculated here:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/methylkit_discussion/8ZrBCzXD5KI

The differential weighing of each sample seems to make this much more difficult.

Best,
Lars

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Confidence intervals
parts:
you can see the difference between weighted means as the difference between two binomial proportions and to calculate the CI of that you can try some of the methods in this paper
http://www.researchgate.net/publication/222405515_Confidence_intervals_for_two_sample_binomial_distribution

Best,
altuna

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Confidence intervals
parts:
you can get CI for the response variable (predicted methylation ratio [between 0 and 1]) from the glm, but it is a bit of a work, and I'm not sure I will implement it in methylKit. 
Here is how you can do it (the section starting with "The code to generate the predicted probabilities (the first line below) is the same as before, except we are also going to ask for standard errors so we can plot a confidence interval"):
http://www.ats.ucla.edu/stat/r/dae/logit.htm

Best,
Altuna
